questions.question_text: Why can an equilateral triangle be constructed for ANY positive side length s > 0?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Sides are s, s, s. Triangle inequality requires s + s > s => 2s > s, which is universally true for all s > 0.

questions.question_text: Two sides of a triangle measure 6 cm and 10 cm. Find the allowable range for the third side x.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Upper bound: x < 6 + 10 = 16 cm. Lower bound: x > 10 - 6 = 4 cm. Range: 4 cm < x < 16 cm.

A surveyor maps roads AB = 12 km, BC = 20 km, AC = 40 km connecting towns A, B, C. Can these towns form a triangular path? Explain.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: AB + BC = 12 + 20 = 32 km. AC = 40 km. Since 32 < 40, sum of two sides is less than third side, violating Triangle Inequality Theorem. They CANNOT form a triangle.

questions.question_text: Find third side bounds for a triangle with sides 8 cm and 15 cm.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Lower bound: 15 - 8 = 7 cm. Upper bound: 15 + 8 = 23 cm. Range: 7 cm < x < 23 cm.

questions.question_text: Explain the geometric compass construction process when attempting to build a triangle with sides 3 cm, 3 cm, 7 cm. Why do compass arcs fail to cross?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Base line AB = 7 cm. Draw arc of radius 3 cm from A and 3 cm from B. Maximum distance reached by both arcs toward each other = 3 + 3 = 6 cm. Since base AB = 7 cm, the arcs leave a 1 cm gap and never intersect, proving no triangle exists.

questions.question_text: An island navigation map marks lighthouses P, Q, R. PQ = 15 miles, QR = 25 miles. Find minimum and maximum possible distance PR if lighthouses form a triangle.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Triangle inequality: PR < PQ + QR => PR < 15 + 25 = 40 miles. Also PR + PQ > QR => PR > 25 - 15 = 10 miles. Range: 10 < PR < 40 miles. Minimum whole distance = 11 miles, maximum = 39 miles.

questions.question_text: A wire of length 30 cm is cut into three integer pieces to form a triangle. If one piece is 14 cm, find all possible integer length combinations for the remaining two pieces.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Longest side = 14 cm. Remaining two sides x + y = 30 - 14 = 16 cm. Inequality constraint: x + y > 14 => 16 > 14 (satisfied). Each side x, y < 14. Pairs (x, y) where x + y = 16 and x, y <= 13: (3, 13), (4, 12), (5, 11), (6, 10), (7, 9), (8, 8).

questions.question_text: Prove that the perimeter of a triangle ABC is greater than the sum of its three medians (or segments from vertices to any internal point O).
questions.marking_scheme_answer: In triangle OAB: OA + OB > AB. In triangle OBC: OB + OC > BC. In triangle OCA: OC + OA > CA. Summing all three inequalities: 2(OA + OB + OC) > AB + BC + CA => OA + OB + OC > 1/2(AB + BC + CA). Also, by applying side triangle comparisons across all vertices, we obtain exact upper and lower perimeter bounds. Thus perimeter exceeds sum of internal node connections.

A triangular park has boundary lengths AB = 100 m, BC = 150 m, CA = 200 m. Verify triangle inequality for all three side pairings.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 1. AB + BC = 100 + 150 = 250 > 200 (CA). Valid. 2. BC + CA = 150 + 200 = 350 > 100 (AB). Valid. 3. CA + AB = 200 + 100 = 300 > 150 (BC). Valid. Park geometry is fully valid.

questions.question_text: Prove that for any quadrilateral ABCD, the sum of all four sides is greater than the sum of its two diagonals AC and BD.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: In triangle ABC: AB + BC > AC. In triangle ADC: AD + DC > AC. Summing: AB + BC + CD + DA > 2AC. Similarly in triangles ABD and BCD: AB + DA > BD and BC + CD > BD => AB + BC + CD + DA > 2BD. Adding both: 2(AB + BC + CD + DA) > 2(AC + BD) => AB + BC + CD + DA > AC + BD.

A carpenter wants to frame a triangular board using three wooden strips of lengths 15 cm, 20 cm, and x cm. List all integer values of x that make the frame scalene.
